subject: Fractional numbers on y-axis in count-based barcharts

messages.author: 6d1cd0a71e6148df
messages.subject: Fractional numbers on y-axis in count-based barcharts
parts:
When there are very few observations in each group, the axis labels for
bar charts are somewhat strange-looking, with decimal numbers (1.0)
instead of integers (1), along with fractional numbers (1.5). Example:

x=c("A","B","B")
qplot(x)

This shows a bar chart with axis breaks at 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0.

qplot(rep(x,2))

This shows a bar chart with axis breaks at 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4.

Could it be changed so that bar charts (i.e., where y=..count..) would
always show integer labels on the y-axis?

In practice you wouldn’t normally plot data with so few oberservations,
but such data can easily occur when you use facetting on a large data
set (which was how I first observed this problem).

--
Karl Ove Hufthammer
